technicalPrinciples.title: How PNG to JPG Conversion Works
technicalPrinciples.description: Understanding the technical process and algorithms behind format conversion

items.title: Transparency Removal & Background Fill
items.description: PNG's alpha channel is removed because JPG doesn't support transparency. Transparent pixels are replaced with a solid background (typically white, configurable to other colors).
benefits: Transparent areas filled with solid color

items.title: Compression Algorithm Conversion
items.description: Switches from PNG's lossless DEFLATE compression to JPG's lossy DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform) compression, achieving 50-80% file size reduction.

items.title: Color Space & Chroma Subsampling
items.description: Converts RGB color data to YCbCr color space and applies chroma subsampling (4:2:0), reducing color information while maintaining perceived brightness.

items.title: Metadata & EXIF Handling
items.description: Optionally transfers EXIF data (camera settings, date, location) and color profiles from PNG to JPG, or removes them to reduce file size by 5-15%.

useCases.title: When & How to Convert PNG to JPG
useCases.description: Common scenarios and best practices for PNG to JPG conversion

items.title: Website Performance Optimization
items.description: Reduce page load times and improve SEO rankings.
items.content: Convert PNG photographs to JPG (quality 85-90) for 50-80% file size reduction. Essential for blogs, portfolios, and content-heavy sites. Use quality 85 for general web images, 90 for hero images. Avoid converting logos or graphics with text - keep those as PNG.

items.title: Social Media & Mobile Sharing
items.description: Faster uploads and better mobile experience.
items.content: Social platforms recompress images anyway, so convert PNG to JPG first (quality 80-85) for control and faster uploads. Especially important on mobile connections. Check for transparency first - if present and needed, use PNG or convert to WebP instead.

items.title: Cloud Storage & Backup
items.description: Save storage space and reduce costs.
items.content: Convert PNG photos to JPG (quality 85-90) to reduce cloud storage by 60-85%. Particularly effective for screenshots mistakenly saved as PNG. Keep originals if you might need lossless quality later - JPG conversion is not reversible.

items.title: Email Attachments
items.description: Stay within size limits while maintaining quality.
items.content: Email services limit attachments to 10-25MB. Convert PNG to JPG at quality 85 to share more images per email. Resize to display dimensions first (e.g., 1920px width) before converting for optimal results and smallest files.

items.title: Photography Workflow
items.content: After editing in software that exports PNG, convert to JPG for delivery. Use quality 90-95 for client work, 85-90 for web publishing. Always resize to final dimensions before converting to avoid wasting quality on unnecessary pixels.

items.title: When NOT to Convert
items.description: Know the limitations to avoid quality issues.
items.content: Don't convert if: 1) Image has transparency you need (logos, graphics), 2) Contains text or sharp edges (screenshots, diagrams), 3) Already small (<50KB), 4) Need pixel-perfect quality. For these cases, keep PNG or use WebP for better compression with lossless/transparency support.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about PNG to JPG conversion

items.question: Will converting PNG to JPG reduce image quality?
items.answer: JPG uses lossy compression, so some quality loss occurs. However, at quality 85-90, the difference is imperceptible to most viewers. PNG to JPG conversion works best for photographs and natural images. Avoid converting graphics with text, logos, or sharp edges as these show visible compression artifacts in JPG.

items.question: What happens to transparency when converting PNG to JPG?
items.answer: JPG does not support transparency. Transparent pixels are automatically filled with a solid background color (typically white). If you need transparency, consider converting to WebP instead, which supports both transparency and better compression than PNG.

items.question: What quality setting should I use for PNG to JPG conversion?
items.answer: Quality 85 is the sweet spot for web use - provides 60-70% file size reduction with minimal visible quality loss. Use 90-95 for professional photography or client work. Use 80 for general web content. Avoid going below 75 as compression artifacts become noticeable.

items.question: Can I convert PNG screenshots to JPG?
items.answer: While technically possible, it's not recommended. PNG is superior for screenshots because it preserves text clarity and sharp edges without artifacts. JPG's lossy compression creates visible blurring around text. Keep screenshots as PNG or convert to WebP lossless for better results.

items.question: Is PNG to JPG conversion reversible?
items.answer: No. JPG compression is lossy - once converted, the discarded data cannot be recovered. Converting JPG back to PNG doesn't restore lost quality, it only changes the container format. Always keep original PNG files if you might need the original quality later.

items.question: How much smaller will my files be after converting PNG to JPG?
items.answer: File size reduction varies by content: photographs typically see 60-80% reduction, complex graphics 40-60%, and simple graphics 30-50%. The exact reduction depends on image complexity, color count, and chosen quality setting. More complex images compress better in JPG.
